definitions.gloss: covered in ~; full of ~; riddled with ~
definitions.explanation: Attaches to nouns to indicate being covered in or full of something undesirable. Almost always carries a negative connotation. Functions as a no-adjective when modifying nouns.

examples.english: My hands are covered in mud.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦レポート→レポート：01543_repooto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧だらけで⟦{出|だ}せない→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: This report is full of mistakes, so I can't submit it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んで→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦{帰|かえ}って→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧きた⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{砂|すな}→砂：00890_suna⟧だらけになっていた。
examples.english: The child who came back from playing in the park had clothes covered in sand.

notes:
FORMS:
Attaches directly to nouns: noun + だらけ
- ⟦{泥|どろ}→泥：03492_doro⟧だらけ (covered in mud)
- ⟦{傷|きず}→傷：02201_kizu⟧だらけ (covered in scratches)
- ⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧だらけ (full of mistakes)
- ⟦{血|ち}→血：01659_chi⟧だらけ (covered in blood)

When modifying a noun, use ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: ⟦{傷|きず}→傷：02201_kizu⟧だらけ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧ (a car covered in scratches).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ～だらけ vs. ～まみれ: Both mean "covered in," but ～まみれ is limited to physical substances (⟦{血|ち}まみれ→血まみれ：14201_chimamire⟧, ⟦{汗|あせ}まみれ→汗まみれ：22902_asemamire⟧) and cannot be used with abstract nouns. ～だらけ works with both physical and abstract things (⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧だらけ, ⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧だらけ).
- ～だらけ vs. ～⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧: ～⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧ means "nothing but" without the negative nuance. ～だらけ always implies the situation is undesirable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{傷|きず}→傷：02201_kizu⟧だらけ (covered in scratches/wounds)
- ⟦{埃|ほこり}→埃：03624_hokori⟧だらけ (covered in dust)
- ⟦{嘘|うそ}→嘘：01796_uso⟧だらけ (full of lies)
- ⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧だらけ (riddled with debt)
